Local TLS patch for go-mitmproxy v1.9.2
====================================

Source: https://github.com/lqqyt2423/go-mitmproxy/tree/v1.9.2 . The original LICENSE and relevant proxy/cert/internal packages (including upstream tests) are preserved. UPSTREAM.json records original file SHA-256 values and the module checksum from root go.sum. The module cache was not edited.

The root go.mod replacement keeps the upstream module identity and version while making this checked-in source authoritative. proxy/proxy.go, proxy/attacker.go, proxy/websocket.go, proxy/entry.go and proxy/connection.go modify upstream source; tls_policy.go, upstream_binding.go and their regression tests are local additions.

Changes: a per-concrete-address TLS configuration callback for normal, alternate HTTP and WSS handshakes; separate authenticated HTTPS-proxy handshakes for alternate HTTP; and CONNECT-host certificate names when IP clients omit SNI. Existing callers without the callback retain upstream options. Skopos supplies verified platform/private-CA trust by default and explicit exact-origin exceptions, with SslInsecure=false.

Client admission: Options.ClientAllowed checks the actual accepted TCP peer before HTTP parsing, CONNECT dialing, certificate work and addons. Rejected connections are closed and the listener continues accepting trusted clients. A nil callback preserves upstream behavior; Skopos always supplies its operator-controlled loopback/default and additional-CIDR policy. No forwarded HTTP header is consulted. The gate applies regardless of capture-routing settings, interception failure or selected upstream proxy.

Listener identity: Options.ListenerAddr publishes the actual bound TCP address before serving and clears it when serving ends. Skopos compares recorder aliases with that socket and pins an owned numeric endpoint before connecting; configured DNS names alone do not establish ownership. This callback preserves existing listener admission and forwarding behavior. Retain its lifecycle when upgrading.

Checked native destinations: Options.UpstreamDialTarget supplies a checked numeric address without changing the logical origin, HTTP Host or TLS ServerName. A bound connection freezes its address/authority/scheme, rechecks its selector before dispatch and refuses lost bindings, changed Host identity, alternate clients and websocket dialers. ConnContext and forwarded-request metadata use distinct typed context keys; pointers to zero-sized structs could alias and overwrite the binding. Skopos privately registers its actual native TCP connection before writing request bytes, keeps revoked bindings until proxy disconnection and retains ordinary behavior for unbound clients. Bound native requests require interception even when a host was previously marked for transparent passthrough.

HTTP/1 lifecycle: upstream closure fully closes an idle downstream connection. An active response drains before the owning HTTP server's StateIdle hook closes that connection, preserving final chunk framing without relying on Windows TCP CloseRead behavior. HTTP/2 retains its separate close path. lifecycle_test.go verifies actual HTTP/HTTPS origin closure during chunked response delivery and safe reconnection. The upstream untrusted-certificate assertion in proxy_test.go now checks x509.UnknownAuthorityError rather than platform-specific wording; the trust requirement and positive TLS control are preserved.

Upgrade procedure: compare these patches against the new upstream release, retain IP SAN and every-connection certificate enforcement, pre-protocol client admission, distinct context keys, checked upstream binding and coordinated HTTP/1 closure, then run the app traffic/enrichment regressions, native binding/capture/Host/SNI/revocation and chunked origin-closure tests, remote-client HTTP/HTTPS/CONNECT/passthrough/WebSocket tests, second-certificate-swap WSS/alternate tests, HTTPS proxy separation test, and upstream WebSocket/SSE/HTTP2 connection tests. Do not remove the replacement based only on a version bump.
